we present a unified end-to-end framework for 3D printing of objects by decoding EEG signals.

(a) we present a unified training framework that combines multi-class Common spatial pattern and deep Convolution Neural Networks to decode visually evoked EEG brain signals; (b) a dynamical graph representation of EEG signals is proposed to accurately capture the spatial correlation between EEG channels in an adaptively manner; and (c) we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by extensive evaluation using offline experiments on two public datasets and through an online system demonstrator.

the development of a novel digital fabrication system which is capable of printing the 3D model of the object that an individual visually concentrates on, by decoding the EEG brain signals.
a new application of BCI technologies, which can potentially help people with visual impairments, as well as the visually normal, to interact with the physical world more efficiently.
the development of an end-to-end system that is able to print 3D objects based on brain signals, and the proposed framework is able to achieve a good tradeoff between the accuracy and efficiency.
